name: Saint Lucia
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting on Saint Lucia: company registry research, citizenship by investment background checks, real estate diligence.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters touching Saint Lucia combines a common law court system with a civil code and property law shaped by French law. Engagements typically involve company and property research, background checks on citizenship by investment holders and developers, and support for litigation before the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court.
intro: Saint Lucia's legal system is unusual within the Eastern Caribbean: it follows English common law in most areas, while its civil code and property law are strongly influenced by French law. The Supreme Court of Judicature, made up of the High Court and the Eastern Caribbean Court of Appeal, hears disputes, and since May 2023 the Caribbean Court of Justice has been Saint Lucia's final appellate court in place of the Privy Council. Companies register with the Registry of Companies and Intellectual Property, which offers e-filing for most services. For investigators, these features mean property and succession questions may turn on civil code concepts, and appellate research must take the change of final court into account.

Organisations commission investigative work involving Saint Lucia mainly in connection with tourism, real estate development and its citizenship by investment programme, established under the Citizenship by Investment Act of 2015. Developers, hotel investors and approved projects attract scrutiny from lenders, purchasers and partners, and individuals holding economic citizenship are sometimes the subject of enhanced due diligence by banks and counterparties abroad. Global business outsourcing is another growing sector. Typical exposures include unverified developer track records, disputes over land title and project funds, undisclosed ownership interests and reputational questions about intermediaries in investment programmes.
legal_system: Saint Lucia has a hybrid legal system: English common law predominates, but the civil code and property law are heavily influenced by French law. The Supreme Court of Judicature, established under the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court arrangements, comprises the High Court and the Eastern Caribbean Court of Appeal. In May 2023 Saint Lucia became the sixth CARICOM member to accept the Caribbean Court of Justice as its final court of appeal. The Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court also supports dispute resolution through court-connected mediation.

data_protection.law: Data Protection Act, No. 11 of 2011 (amended 2015), partly in force since 31 January 2023
data_protection.summary: Saint Lucia's Data Protection Act No. 11 of 2011 provides for a Data Protection Commissioner, data protection principles and rules on transfers of personal data abroad. Statutory Instrument 4 of 2023 brought parts of the Act into force on 31 January 2023, including the data protection principles; we have not confirmed whether the remaining provisions have commenced or whether the Commissioner's office is operating. Investigations collecting personal data about individuals in Saint Lucia should therefore have a documented lawful purpose, limit collection and plan any transfer with Saint Lucian counsel. TDSC applies minimisation, secure storage and controlled retention throughout.

investigator_regulation: We have not identified, from official sources available to us, a dedicated licensing regime for private investigators in Saint Lucia. The lawfulness of any local investigative step, including surveillance, recording and approaches to witnesses or officials, should be confirmed with Saint Lucian counsel before it is taken. Because inquiries in a small jurisdiction are quickly noticed, discretion is a practical as well as legal concern. TDSC therefore conducts most research from Nashville and uses appropriately qualified local professionals only for steps agreed with counsel.
corporate_records: Companies are registered with the Registry of Companies and Intellectual Property, constituted under the Companies and Intellectual Property Registry Act, which offers e-filing for most services, although registration fees are paid in person. International business companies are formed under separate legislation. Businesses must also register with the Inland Revenue Department and the National Insurance Corporation, and non-CARICOM nationals holding more than 49 percent of a company's shares require a trade licence. We have not confirmed what shareholder, director or beneficial ownership information is publicly searchable. Land title and civil code property records are usually researched with local counsel.
anti_corruption: The Integrity in Public Life Act of 2004 governs official conduct and declarations through the Integrity Commission, and special prosecutor legislation allows action against officials for misuse of state resources. The Money Laundering (Prevention) Act (Cap. 12.20) and the Proceeds of Crime Act (Cap. 3.04) form the core AML framework, with the Financial Intelligence Authority, established under 2002 legislation, receiving suspicious transaction reports. The Royal Saint Lucia Police Force and the Director of Public Prosecutions enforce. Saint Lucia acceded to the UN Convention against Corruption in 2011.

matters.title: Hotel and resort developer diligence
matters.text: Background research on developers, sponsors and contractors behind tourism and real estate projects, including projects approved for investment programmes, examining prior developments, litigation, insolvencies, ownership and media, for lenders, purchasers, operators and equity partners.

matters.title: Economic citizenship background checks
matters.text: Enhanced due diligence on individuals who hold Saint Lucian citizenship under the 2015 programme, focusing on identity history, business record, litigation, sanctions exposure and media in the countries where they actually reside and conduct business.

matters.title: Land and property disputes
matters.text: Supporting counsel in disputes over land title, family property and project land, where French-influenced civil code concepts apply, through chronology building, corporate and party research and identification of related entities and transactions.

matters.title: Outsourcing partner verification
matters.text: Verifying the ownership, management and track record of business process outsourcing and service providers based in Saint Lucia before contracts are awarded, including checks for related parties, litigation and adverse media.

matters.title: Public project integrity questions
matters.text: Research for counsel and compliance teams into counterparties in infrastructure and public projects where integrity concerns have been raised, using published judgments, procurement information, corporate records and media, while distinguishing allegations from established findings.

tdsc_approach: TDSC scopes Saint Lucia engagements from Nashville with attention to the island's hybrid legal tradition, since property and family questions may turn on civil code concepts while procedure follows common law. Research draws on registry information, published Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court and Caribbean Court of Justice judgments, foreign filings, project and procurement information and regional media. Because the Data Protection Act 2011 has been brought into force only in part, TDSC applies its principles together with its own minimisation and retention standards and confirms handling with Saint Lucian counsel where personal data is gathered locally. Local inquiries are used sparingly, agreed with counsel and carried out by appropriately qualified professionals. TDSC does not hold a Saint Lucian licence and does not provide legal advice.

faqs.q: Why does French law matter in Saint Lucia?
faqs.a: Saint Lucia's civil code and property law are heavily influenced by French law, even though most other areas follow English common law. Disputes over land, inheritance and family property can therefore involve concepts unfamiliar to common law practitioners. TDSC frames research on these matters with Saint Lucian counsel.

faqs.q: What is Saint Lucia's final court of appeal?
faqs.a: Since May 2023 the Caribbean Court of Justice has been Saint Lucia's final appellate court, replacing the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council. Earlier cases may have gone to the Privy Council, so litigation research covers both, as well as the High Court and the Eastern Caribbean Court of Appeal.

faqs.q: Can TDSC check the background of a Saint Lucian citizenship by investment holder?
faqs.a: Yes, through lawful public sources. Programme files are confidential and we do not seek them. We research identity history, corporate roles, litigation, sanctions exposure and media, mainly in the countries where the person lives and works, and report findings with clear sourcing.

faqs.q: How do you research a developer behind a Saint Lucia resort project?
faqs.a: We review the developer's corporate history in Saint Lucia and elsewhere, previous projects and their outcomes, litigation and insolvency records, related companies and principals, and media coverage. Where a site visit or local inquiry would add value, it is planned with counsel and conducted by qualified local professionals.

faqs.q: Is there a public beneficial ownership register in Saint Lucia?
faqs.a: We have not confirmed that beneficial ownership information is publicly searchable in Saint Lucia. Ownership is therefore usually established from registry documents available through lawful channels, litigation, foreign filings and other sources, and we state the confidence level of any conclusion.
